bug_description.normalized: PEM_read_bio compares stack buffer bytes with strncmp before ensuring the bytes after the short line returned by BIO_gets are initialized, so a malformed PEM line can make the header check read uninitialized stack data.

source.value_from: attacker-controlled BIO contents from the fuzz input are copied into stack buffer buf and the returned character count i determines which prefix was initialized
source.description: PEM_read_bio first materializes attacker-controlled line data into the local stack buffer and learns how many bytes BIO_gets actually initialized.

sink.description: strncmp consumes 11 bytes from buf while testing for a PEM begin marker, so it can read uninitialized stack bytes left past the short line returned by BIO_gets.

root_cause.description: After a short BIO_gets result, the code only writes a newline and terminator after the initialized prefix and never initializes the intervening bytes that strncmp later reads up to byte 10.

parser_admitted.description: The sample reaches the PEM header-recognition branch in PEM_read_bio; this is the parser gate for an accepted begin-line candidate.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker controls the bytes copied into buf and whether BIO_gets returns fewer than 11 initialized bytes.

coarse_trace.summary: PEM_read_bio reads an attacker-controlled line from the BIO into stack buffer buf and uses it as the candidate PEM header line.
The function normalizes trailing whitespace by adjusting i and appending '\n' and '\0', but it does not initialize any bytes between the short BIO_gets prefix and those terminators.
The header test uses strncmp(buf, "-----BEGIN ", 11), which reads past the initialized prefix and triggers MSAN on uninitialized stack bytes.

fine_trace.note: PEM_read_bio copies the next attacker-controlled line from the BIO into stack buffer buf and returns in i how many bytes were initialized by that read.

The loop trims trailing whitespace from the initialized prefix and can leave i below 10 when the attacker supplied a short or whitespace-only line, so bytes buf[i+1] through buf[10] remain whatever was already on the stack.
The code writes only a newline and terminator after the trimmed prefix; it still leaves any gap between the short initialized prefix and byte 10 of buf uninitialized.
The begin-line check always reads 11 bytes from buf; when step 3 left part of that range uninitialized, strncmp consumes those stale stack bytes and MSAN reports the uninitialized read here.

poc.trigger: Feed PEM_read_bio a BIO line shorter than the 11-byte "-----BEGIN " probe so the stack buffer is only partially initialized before the header comparison.

format.name: PEM-like text line
format.contract: The witness input must cause the first line read by PEM_read_bio to be shorter than 11 bytes, or trimmed down below that length, before the function executes strncmp(buf, "-----BEGIN ", 11).
